prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Columbus Ohio for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single universally “best” dentist for implants in Columbus — the right provider depends on your case (simple single implant vs full-arch reconstruction), your medical history, and whether you need surgery and/or complex restorative work. Here’s how to find the best clinician for you and next steps I can help with.

Which type of provider to consider
- Oral & maxillofacial surgeons (OMS): surgical specialists who handle complex extractions, bone grafts and implant placement.  
- Periodontists: gum and bone specialists who often place implants, especially when bone grafting is needed.  
- Prosthodontists: specialists in restoring teeth and fabricating implant crowns/bridges; ideal when the restorative result is critical.  
- General dentists with advanced implant training (fellowship/continuing education) — fine for straightforward cases.

How to choose a top provider
- Board-certified or specialty-trained: look for OMFS (AAOMS), periodontists (AAP) or prosthodontists (ACP).  
- Experience with cases like yours: ask how many similar implants they place per year and whether they handle the restoration or coordinate with a prosthodontist.  
- Use of modern diagnostics: CBCT (3D) imaging, guided/digital planning.  
- Evidence of quality: before/after photos, patient testimonials, online reviews, and willingness to provide references.  
- Clear written treatment plan and cost breakdown (surgery, grafting, implant, abutment, crown), predicted timeline, and follow-up care.  
- Collaborative care: team approach (surgeon + restorative clinician) is a plus for complex work.

Questions to ask at a consult
- Which specialist will place the implant and who will restore it?  
- What implant system do you use and why?  
- How many implants like mine have you placed? What’s your complication/failure rate?  
- Do I need bone grafting or sinus lift? If so, how does that change timeline and cost?  
- Do you use CBCT and guided surgery? Will you show me the digital plan?  
- What sedation options do you offer?  
- What is the total cost and payment/financing options? Any warranty or maintenance plan?

Warning signs
- No imaging or vague answers about the procedure.  
- Pressuring you to choose the cheapest implant without clear reasoning.  
- No follow-up plan or unclear responsibility between surgeon and restorative dentist.  
- Very poor or mixed online reviews and unwillingness to provide before/after photos or references.

Where to search
- AAOMS.org (oral surgeons)  
- AAID.org (implant dentists)  
- ADA Find-a-Dentist and local dental society referrals  
- Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center / OSU College of Dentistry (for specialists and complex cases)  
- Local patient reviews (Google, Healthgrades) — treat reviews as one data point.

If you want, I can:
- Look up well-reviewed implant specialists in Columbus if you give a ZIP code or neighborhood.  
- Provide a short checklist you can bring to consults.

Which would you prefer?
